A long but interesting piece on the overconfidence of the incompetent, by David Dunning (of Dunning-Kruger fame).

Whenever I read anything on the subject of David Dunning's work in human incompetence I can't help but wonder if he is really an authority on this or not. I mean if you take his research and apply it on top of the man, well how does David know he is not falling into the very effect that bears his name? Can one truly be authoritative on a subject such as human behavior and psychology when there is no truly empirical grounding in it? I'm sure someone will argue with me on this, and thus we will prove to both show our incompetence in these areas, but nevertheless it fascinates me that anyone can lay claim to the position of determiner of human incompetence. It's much the same as when debating with someone who knows all the logical fallacies by heart and counters every point you make by labeling it "xyz fallacy". They can go so many levels of meta on that so in the end it seems like there is nothing but fallacious thinking and no actual truth, facts or reality. It really makes me wonder if there is any way to call anyone authoritative in any subject if you consider Dunning-Kruger and the incompleteness of human knowledge and understanding. Perhaps we're all idiots and just don't know it.
